steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix brown sugar, rice vinegar, maple syrup, and black pepper in a small bowl.
Place bacon slices on a cooling rack set over a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes, turn slices, and bake another 5 minutes.
Remove bacon and brush both sides with brown sugar mixture.
Return bacon to the oven and bake another 5 minutes.
Repeat basting every 5 minutes until bacon is browned and crisp, about 35 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Candied Bacon
raw_recipe.description: To make candied bacon, Chef John bakes thick center-cut bacon with a brown sugar, vinegar, and maple syrup glaze for a sweet and smoky party snack.
raw_recipe.name: Candied Bacon

review.reviewBody: Candied bacon is exactly right! It took an hour to get to the point of doneness in my photo, and that was turning it up for the last 15 minutes. I did everything that was listed in the recipe, and the results were worth it. Interesting. I had a package of bacon that weighed 1.25 pounds, and half I used for this and half I fried as usual. The ingredients for the candied part was just right for that amount of bacon. The saltiness of the regularly fried bacon was so pronounced after tasting the candied bacon! We had friends over for brunch, and the guys preferred the regular, but we gals loved the candied. We were thinking of cutting the bacon in half, skewering it on pretty little sticks, and serving it for a party. Trust me, it would be a hit! Thanks again, as usual, Chef John!

Cook time does need adjustment.
Use only thick cut bacon as the recipe states, but...
Cook each side to start for 10 min per.
Remove and baste each side and cook for 10 min at a a time.
This allows the moisture from the Maple syrup and vinegar to evaporate and get the fat to render and get a good sticky coating.
Repeat the baste, and flip for as many cycles it takes to create a beautiful dark brown bacon in 10 min cycles. It took me about 4 or 5 cycles after the the basting had begun. 
I would add more brown sugar to the mix for some more sweet sticky goodness.
There is enough basting liquid in the recipe. if you run out, just continue the cooking and it should be plenty to make a wonderful bacon treat.

I've made this a few times now. Always use thick cut bacon, thinner bacon just won't hold up under the glaze. I also doubled the glaze. I use a rack in a sheet pan, essential to getting the bacon crisp. Liberal basting is key to a good crust. Let the bacon cook until the fat starts to render before you start basting. This year I used a spice rub prior to cooking. The rub I Used is called Fatboy's sweet rub. I sprinkled it on one side of the bacon before it went into the oven. It gave the bacon a little more depth of flavor. After the last baste, leave the bacon in until it is a deep mahogany color. After it comes out, let it cool just a bit before you plate it. I used a fish spatula to get it off the rack, it was a little bit of work but it came off ok. Plate it before the glaze sets a bit and it will become soggy. If you're going to let it set a bit before eating, stack it with parchment between the layers; that keeps the pieces separate and lets the glaze dry out more. It's always a hit when I bring it.

Wow! This was awesome! Couldn't stop eating it. Used bourbon in place of rice vinegar and made a double batch of the baste, as others suggested. Placed parchment paper under the rack and lightly coated rack with cooking spray to help with cleanup. To cut down on time involved, would suggest cooking the bacon for at least 20 minutes before putting on the first baste. Also turned the oven temp up to 375 and it didn't seem to alter the end result on the second batch.....still awesome just a bit quicker to the end result and enjoying it. Bacon sets up as it cools to become more of a bacon stick. Any bacon lover will enjoy this ..... Yummmmmm!!!!!!

The only ingredient I changed was the cut of bacon. I made this in my GoWISEusa air fryer. 400 degrees F for 12 minutes total. I started by cutting the bacon in half and air frying it for 2 minutes, turned it over for 2 more minutes and then started turning and basting every 2 minutes.

Here are a few suggestions:
A little less than 1 lb (thick cut) fit on my oven rack. 
Lining the baking tray in foil is a super good idea for easy clean-up.
I doubled the sugar and syrup, but not the vinegar.
Use a basing brush to apply the glaze.
Don't flip and baste the bacon every 5 minutes. That's way too much work and you will lose most of your glaze if you flip too quick. I flipped and glazed about every 10-15 minutes. Using thick cut bacon, I think I flipped the bacon 3 times, so a total bake time of less than 1 hour.
Last suggestion, let the bacon sit and cool completely (30 mins?). It was much better after the sugar hardened a little bit.

Easy alteration for this recipe is to layer the cookie sheet with glaze then bacon then top with more glaze. That way there's no basting every 5 minutes I just cooked the bacon coated in the glaze for 35 minutes and it's done and delicious. I also quadrupled the glaze recipe after reading other people's reviews.
I went through double the ingredients on 1.5 lbs of bacon. I used regular thick cut bacon, but I will purchase bacan twice as thick next time.

Oh, baby, this was good. Yes, labor intensive, and as other reviewers suggested, increase the thickness of the goo to make a paste vs. a liquid, as we also ran out and had to make more. Also baste and flip maybe every 10-15 minutes, vs. 5, but do keep an eye on. Worth the work. I even had to use normal thin-sliced bacon and it was fantastic. Making it for the second time today! :)

I’ve made two batches of this yummy candied bacon. I did switch up the second batch a bit and used 1 tablespoon maple syrup and 1 tablespoon of Mikes Hot Honey. I also sprinkled the black pepper on prior to the first unglazed baking. After it was glazed, I sprinkled a very small amount of red pepper flakes to give a slight zing. Both the recipe as is and my modes made a wonderful treat for a party they were taken to.

Added approx 1-1/2 teaspoon of sandwich mustard instead of rice vinegar, and marinated overnight in 1/2 of the baste in refrigerator. Then cooked in oven as directed. It was awesome! Served with crepes and waffles when I had overnight quests! It was a huge hit!
This bacon was a big hit at the Christmas party. I used extra thick cut maple flavored bacon. It did take a long time to bake with constant basting and turning, but it was so worth it.
Amazing. So good. You do have to double the glaze and expect longer than 45 minutes. Maybe an hour. Still worth it.

Cooking bacon on a rack takes 3-4 times longer than baking in the sheet pan due to no grease to cook in. Recommend partial 3/4 cook before putting on rack and basting.

I have been making candied bacon for years and this is, without fail, my go-to recipe. The rice vinegar is crucial and makes all the difference. I would personally recommend thick-cut bacon, and doubling the amount of candy mixture. Other recipes call for simply sprinkling brown sugar over raw bacon then baking it. Compared to that, this recipe may seem rather labor-intensive, but it is well worth it. This candied bacon is exactly right. My family friends love it so much that I have been pressured to start selling it LOL.
I’ve made this several times just as described. It’s delicious and is always hit when company visits our home. Usually disappears the first day regardless of how much I make. Definitely a keeper!

OMG!! There's a restaurant in our area that serves this bacon with their Sunday brunch. This is served as a standard feature with their Bloody Mary bar option (along with jumbo shrimp) that is to die for. Yes, both treats come with their Bloody Mary. But this bacon is soooo good!
